title: Discourse and Subject Position Laboratory
summary: Eight undisputed events in a fictional woman's six months with a community day service, written up five times: as a case note, a risk register entry, an advocacy bulletin, a recovery-oriented discharge summary and a commissioning report. For each account the learner identifies the subject position it produces, the action it makes legitimate, who it authorises to speak and where responsibility lands, with every wrong option being the right answer for a different account. The ledger of events stays on screen throughout, and one entry in it - the decision that halved the programme's hours - appears in only one of the five accounts.
learningObjectives: Identify the subject position an account makes available to the person it is about.
Say which actions a given position renders reasonable and which unreasonable.
Name who an account authorises to say what is happening.
Trace where responsibility is placed by a description that never mentions responsibility.
Explain why analysing discourse is neither word-counting nor a claim that events are made of language.
interactionTypes: account switching with a pinned text
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; the tool asks nothing about the person using it and produces no score for anyone.
accessibilityNotes: Native radios and buttons only; no dragging and no timing. The account being analysed is the pinned primary result at 209px, so its full text stays beside the four questions while they are answered and while the controls column is scrolled. The ledger entry that only one account mentions is marked with a heavier rule and an explanatory phrase in text, so it is never identified by colour alone. Wrong answers explain which account the chosen option is the correct answer for, rather than reporting an error. Headings do not skip. Changes are announced through the shell's polite live region; reduced motion honoured; forced-colours rules provided; usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Same events, five write-ups: subject positions, legitimacy, authority and where responsibility comes to rest
simulationNotes: R, the service, the assessment and all five accounts are invented for teaching; no real person, service, record or document is reproduced and nothing here is a clinical description of anybody. There is no random generation and no seed. Each account carries an authored answer to each of the four analytic dimensions, and the option set for each dimension contains exactly one correct answer per account, so every distractor is the right answer for a different text. The ledger is fixed and every account is consistent with all eight entries: none of the five contains a false statement, which is why accuracy cannot be what separates them. Entry 2, the halving of the programme's hours, appears only in the advocacy bulletin; the other four genres have no field for it, which is the tool's central structural point rather than an accusation of concealment.
